PullRequest.Title: sessions: Compact the mark-as-done nudge after repeated use
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Reduce the space occupied by the merged-PR nudge once users are familiar with it.

- Persist successful nudge actions per profile and show the compact version after the third use. Dismissals, failed actions, and archiving outside the nudge do not count.
- Keep the merge icon and existing PR-merged label on the left, with **Mark as Done** (or **Archive**), **Configure**, and dismiss aligned on the right. When space is limited, the buttons wrap together below the title while dismiss stays at the top right.
- Hide the explanatory body in compact mode, truncate the title with a hover at narrow widths, and preserve keyboard order, focused controls, and existing callbacks.
- Add normal-width and narrow compact fixtures with dark/light variants, plus accessibility help and regression coverage.

## Validation

- Targeted nudge service and widget suites: **81 passing**.
- `npm run transpile-client` and `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- ESLint, CSS lint, targeted hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Rendered compact fixtures in dark/light themes at normal and narrow widths; verified no overflow, right-aligned actions, and Tab order.

### Responsive-layout follow-up

- Verified the exact content-based wrap threshold, focus retention, keyboard order, and top-right dismiss placement.
- Targeted widget suite: **37 passing**. Targeted hygiene and whitespace checks passed.
- Captured updated narrow fixtures in dark and light themes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the archive/mark-as-done nudge for the visible primary session and restore compact mode across reloads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Eligibility and merged-state resolution must complete before the nudge appears. Existing GitHub pull-request models refresh before the merged state is known; the diff then performs one synchronous profile-storage cache lookup while mapping the already-resolved state. The storage lookup does not add network, IPC, filesystem, or database work to this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch pull-request metadata and reviews from GitHub to establish that each distinct PR is merged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two parallel HTTP requests per distinct owner/repository/PR key on an initial refresh; distinct references are shared, concurrent refreshes for one key are coalesced, and one poller per shared model repeats every 60 seconds while observed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model references, refresh calls, request cardinality, ETag reuse, and polling existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial responses are required to produce the merged state and show the nudge; later polls update it asynchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of distinct PR keys after Map deduplication across session artifacts and workspace associations; compact-state work remains O(1) regardless of PR count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each model coalesces concurrent refreshes with _refreshPromise; PR metadata and reviews run as a pair in parallel, while distinct deduplicated PR keys may refresh concurrently. The new cached count read adds no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR models are shared by key, in-flight refreshes are coalesced, warm requests use ETags, and polling is shared per model. Profile storage is loaded into an in-memory Map, so cold and warm compact-count reads are both local after storage-service initialization; external changes invalidate only the mapped options.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the observable dependency and storage implementation show the new read is in-memory, while the network path is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub latency and the number of PRs vary, but those costs are pre-existing and unchanged. The added local cache lookup is constant-time.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds only an O(1) cached read after existing merged-state work and does not increase PR request frequency, cardinality, or polling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successfully archive or mark a session as done through the nudge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing onboarding flow and provider archive call complete first. The diff then reads the in-memory count and synchronously records one new cached value before telemetry and action completion; durable storage flushing is delayed and off the action's awaited critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Archive the selected session through its provider; provider-dependent implementations may dispatch to an agent host or remote connection and may update detached-worktree state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider archive operation per successful button action, guarded against duplicate clicks by the widget's archiving flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The nudge already awaited exactly one provider archive operation before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited and therefore on the action critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most three changed values over the profile lifetime; subsequent stores of the capped value are suppressed by Storage.set before events or persistence. Changed writes are coalesced by the storage flush delayer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the in-memory Map mutation and scheduling are synchronous; the database update is delayed and not awaited by the action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Successful nudge actions, capped at three state transitions. Work after the threshold remains an O(1) cache read plus an unchanged-value check with no durable write.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One action per widget is allowed at a time. Cross-window storage updates can interleave, but changed writes are accumulated by the storage layer; there is no burst proportional to sessions or PRs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The count is read from the initialized profile-storage cache. Values 1-3 trigger delayed persistence and observable invalidation; value 3 is a stable positive state, and repeated attempts are deduplicated before flushing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed archive lines, storage cache, unchanged-value early return, and delayed flush are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider archive cost varies by provider, but its placement and multiplicity are unchanged. New persistence is bounded to three actual writes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only introduced boundary is bounded to three coalesced background writes and does not add awaited I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, resize, and update the compact archive nudge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The options autorun calls setSessionArchiveNudge, which updates one existing widget synchronously. The compact path changes text/hidden/classes and reparents the two-button footer only when compact mode transitions; browser layout then occurs normally. Hover UI is created only after mouse-over and delay.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed-size widget with one title, body, two buttons, and dismiss action; update cost does not scale with transcript length, session count, or PR count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM updates run synchronously on the UI thread for the single visible chat input. There are no loops, queues, frame callbacks, or concurrent tasks introduced by compact rendering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The widget instance and controls are reused across option changes. The footer is reparented only when its required parent changes, and the registered delayed-hover listeners/map entry are disposed with the widget.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed widget and CSS code contain fixed DOM mutations only; geometry reads are confined to tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/layout cost depends on host width, but the DOM is fixed and no changed production code reads geometry or forces a read-after-write layout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff does not introduce forced synchronous layout, per-frame work, repeated reconstruction, or retained widget resources.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The help provider reads the existing configuration value and appends one localized string while constructing help content.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one additional localized paragraph per help invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous invocation when accessibility help is requested; no asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retained collection is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk is a single conditional content append.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added operation is constant-sized string assembly.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added fixed text does not create meaningful CPU, allocation, I/O, or lifecycle growth.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced compact-state storage, observable invalidation, widget update/layout and hover cleanup, PR refresh/polling, provider archive boundaries, and accessibility help. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.
